questions.q: The locus of the point of intersection of the lines $x=a \left(\frac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}\right)$ and $y=\frac{2 a t}{1+t^2}$represent $(t$ being a parameter)
questions.solution:
Given $x=a \left(\frac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}\right)$ and $ y=\frac{2 a t}{1+t^2}\begin{aligned}$& $\text{ Let } \quad$ t=\tan $\theta$\\
& \Rightarrow \quad x=a$\left(\frac{1-\tan ^2 \theta}{1+\tan ^2 \theta}\right)$\\
& $\text{ and } \quad$ y=$\frac{2 a \tan \theta}{1+\tan ^2 \theta}$\\
& \Rightarrow \quad x=a \cos 2 $\theta \text{ and }$ y=a \sin 2 $\theta$\\
& \Rightarrow \cos 2 $\theta=\frac{x}{a} \text{ and } \sin2 $\theta=$\frac{y}{a}$
\end{aligned}
Squaring both sides, we get
$\cos ^2 2 $\theta=$\frac{x^2}{a^2}$....(i)
and
$\sin ^2 2 $\theta=$\frac{y^2}{a^2}$....(ii)
Adding Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
 \begin{aligned}
\quad $\cos ^2 2 \theta+\sin ^2 2 $\theta$& =\frac{x^2}{a^2}+\frac{y^2}{a^2}$\\
\Rightarrow \quad x²+y² & =a²
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Locus is a circle having centre at origin and radius $a$.$

questions.q: What is the angle between the two straight lines $y=(2-\sqrt{3}) x+5$ and $y=(2+\sqrt{3}) x-7 ?$
questions.solution:
The given lines are:
$y=(2-\sqrt{3}) x+5 \text{ and } y=(2+\sqrt{3}) x-7$
Therefore, slope of first line $=m_1=2-\sqrt{3}$ and slope of second line $=m_2=2+\sqrt{3}$
$\therefore \quad \tan \theta=\left|\frac{m_2-m_1}{1+m_1 m_2}\right|=\left|\frac{2+\sqrt{3}-2+\sqrt{3}}{1+(4-3)}\right|$
$=\left|\frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{2}\right|=\sqrt{3}=\tan \frac{\pi}{3} \Rightarrow \theta=\frac{\pi}{3}=60^{{}^{\circ}}$

questions.q: The larger of two angles made with the $X$-axis of a straight line drawn through $(1,2)$ so that it intersects the line $x + y = 4$ at a point distant $\sqrt{6} / 3$ from the point $(1,2)$ is
questions.solution:
Let $A = (1,2)$ equation of line is

$\dfrac{x - 1}{cos\theta} = \dfrac{y - 2}{sin\theta} = r = \dfrac{6}{3}$

$∴ x = \dfrac{6}{3}cos\theta + 1, y = \dfrac{6}{3}sin\theta + 2$

This point lies on line $x + y = 4$

$∴ \dfrac{6}{3}cos\theta + \dfrac{6}{3}sin\theta = 1$

$⇒ sin\theta + cos\theta = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \theta\right) = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\pi}{4} + \theta = 60 °$ or $120 °$

$⇒ \theta = 15 °$ or $75 °$

$∴$ Larger angle $= 75 °$

questions.q: Straight lines $3x + 4y = 5 and 4x - 3y = 15$~intersect at the point $A$. If point $B and C$ are chosen on these two lines such that $AB = AC$, then the possible equation of the line $BC$ passing through the point $\left(1, 2\right)$ is
questions.solution:
The given straight lines are $3x + 4y = 5 and 4x - 3y = 15$. Clearly, these straight lines are perpendicular to each other $\left({m}_{1}{m}_{2} = - 1\right)$ and intersect at A$. Now, $B and C$ are points on these lines such that $AB = AC and BC$ passes through \left(1, 2\right).

From figure it is clear that $∠ B = ∠ C = 45 °$

Let slope of $BC$ be $m$. Then,

$tan45 ° = $\left|\dfrac{m + \dfrac{3}{4}}{1 - \dfrac{3}{4}m}\right|$

$⇒ \pm 1 = \dfrac{4m + 3}{4 - 3m}$

$4m + 3 = \pm \left(4 - 3m\right)

$4m + 3 = 4 - 3m$

or $4m + 3 = - 4 + 3m$

$m = $\dfrac{1}{7}$

or $m = - 7$

Hence, equation of $BC$ is

$y - 2 = \dfrac{1}{7}\left(x - 1\right)

or $y - 2 = - 7 $\left(x - 1\right)$

$⇒ 7y - 14 = x - 1$

or $y - 2 = - 7x + 7$

$⇒ x - 7y + 13 = 0$

or $7x + y - 9 = 0$

Hence, option (c) is correct.

Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.q: Two equal sides of an isosceles triangle are $7x - y + 3 = 0$ and $x + y - 3 = 0$ and its third side passes through the point $( 1, - 10 )$. The equation of the third side is
questions.solution:
The third side is parallel to a bisector of the angle between equal sides.

The bisectors are $\dfrac{7x - y + 3}{{7}^{2} + \left(- 1\right)^{2}} = \pm \dfrac{( x + y - 3 )}{{1}^{2} + {1}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{7x - y + 3}{5\sqrt{2}} = \pm \dfrac{( x + y - 3 )}{2}$

$⇒ 7x - y + 3 = \pm 5 ( x + y - 3 )$

$⇒ 2x - 6y + 18 = 0$ or $12x + 4y - 12 = 0$

$⇒ x - 3y + 9 = 0$ or $3x + y - 3 = 0$

Let the third side be $x - 3y = k$ or $3x + y = L$

It passes through $( 1, - 10 )$.

$⇒ k = 31, L = - 7$

Hence, required lines are $x - 3y = 31$ or $3x + y = - 7$.&

questions.solution:
The equations of the lines are



$\begin{array}{l}$$\mathrm{p}_{1} \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{q}_{1} \mathrm{y}-$1=0 \\

$\mathrm{p}_{2} \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{q}_{2} \mathrm{y}-$1=0

\end{array}



and $\mathrm{p}_{3} \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{q}_{3} \mathrm{y}-1=0$

As they are concurrent,



$\left|\begin{array}{lll}

\mathrm{p}_{1}$& $\mathrm{q}_{1}$& -1 \\

$\mathrm{p}_{2}$& $\mathrm{q}_{2}$& -1 \\

$\mathrm{p}_{3}$& $\mathrm{q}_{3}$& -1

\end{array}\right|=0 \Rightarrow$\left|\begin{array}{lll}

\mathrm{p}_{1}$& $\mathrm{q}_{1}$& 1 \\

$\mathrm{p}_{2}$& $\mathrm{q}_{2}$& 1 \\

$\mathrm{p}_{3}$& $\mathrm{q}_{3}$& 1

\end{array}\right|=0



This is also the condition for the points $\left(\mathrm{p}_{1}, \mathrm{q}_{1}\right),\left(\mathrm{p}_{2}, \mathrm{q}_{2}\right)$ and $\left(\mathrm{p}_{3}, \mathrm{q}_{3}\right)$ to be collinear.

questions.q: If \(\mathrm{m}\) arithmetic means are inserted between 1 and 31 so that the ratio of the \(7^{\text{th }}\) and \((\mathrm{m}-1)^{\text{th }}\) means is \(5: 9\), then find the value of \(m\).
questions.solution:
Let the means be \(x_1, x_2, \ldots \ldots x_m\) so that \(1, \mathrm{x}_{1},  \mathrm{x}}_{2}, \ldots . \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{m}},31\) is an A.P. of \((\mathrm{m}+2)\) terms.
Now, \(31=\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{m}+2}=\mathrm{a}+(\mathrm{m}+1) \mathrm{d}=1+(\mathrm{m}+1) \mathrm{d}\)
\(\therefore \mathrm{d}=\frac{30}{\mathrm{ m}+1}\) Given : \(\frac{\mathrm{x}_7}{\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{m}-1}}=\frac{5}{9}\)
$$\begin{aligned}& \therefore \frac{\mathrm{T}_8}{\mathrm{ T}_{\mathrm{m}}}=\frac{\mathrm{a}+7 \mathrm{ d}}{\mathrm{a}+(\mathrm{m}-1) \mathrm{d}}=\frac{5}{9}\\
& \Rightarrow 9 \mathrm{a}+63 \mathrm{ d}=5 \mathrm{a}+(5 \mathrm{ m}-5) \mathrm{d}\\
& \Rightarrow 4.1=(5 \mathrm{ m}-68) \frac{30}{\mathrm{ m}+1}\\
& \Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{ m}+2=75 \mathrm{ m}-1020 \Rightarrow 73 \mathrm{ m}=1022 \\
& \therefore \quad \mathrm{m}=\frac{1022}{73}=14
\end{aligned}$$\)
